messages:
oliver: Heads-up — proposal to change our API key format from 32 -> 48 bytes for better entropy. We need a migration plan that doesn't break existing customers. Who has thoughts on compatibility shims?

maria: Dual-read mode seems safest: accept both old and new keys for a transition window, log usage, and then cut off old keys after X days. Also rotate internal keys we control. :thinking:

jin: Dual-read ok, but watch caching/proxy layers — some edge proxies cache 401s. We should make the shim idempotent and return consistent errors.

casey: We could implement a lightweight shim service that exchanges legacy keys for short-lived JWTs. Downstream services validate JWTs only — no code change needed for most services.

oliver: Prototype exchange flow (sketch):
```
POST /v1/auth/exchange
Request: { "api_key": "sk-..." }
Response: { "access_token": "eyJ..", "expires_in": 3600, "legacy_key": true }
```
Shim stores mapping in a scoped cache (ttl ~1h) and emits telemetry on each exchange.

maria: Telemetry: tag requests with `legacy_key=true|false`, `migration_participant=shim`, and org_id. We need dashboards for top legacy users so SEs can help.

jin: RBAC question: current legacy keys are org-scoped. New model supports project-scoped keys and finer grants. Migration must preserve existing permissions until customer acts.

casey: Proposal: map legacy org keys -> implicit `project:*` within their org for the migration window. After cutover, require explicit project binding; provide a UI to split keys into project-scoped tokens.

oliver: Service auth: a lot of CI jobs and cron tasks use API keys. We should provide a service-principal mint flow so infra can get short-lived tokens instead of long-lived keys.

maria: SDK helpers: `redwood.auth.exchangeLegacyKey(oldKey)` and `redwood.auth.mintServiceToken(sp_id)` — implement in our JS/Go libs. Also docs on rotating keys in CI.

jin: Tradeoffs: Longer transition reduces customer disruption but extends attack surface and support burden. Recommend 60 days with a hard cut, email cadence at 30/14/7/1 days.

casey: Also enforce rate limits at token level post-exchange so legacy keys can't bypass the new quotas. Add an allowlist for a small set of enterprise customers if needed.

deploy-bot: deploy: shim v0.1 canary -> staging at 10:30 PST :rocket:

oliver: Next steps: write a short RFC that includes shim design, RBAC mapping table, migration timeline (60d), telemetry dashboards, and a rollback plan. Who volunteers to draft?

maria: I'll draft the RFC today and ping @jin to help with the RBAC mapping and sample data.

jin: Happy to help. I'll pull the key usage tables and produce mapping examples.

casey: I'll prototype the shim exchange endpoint and a cache invalidation plan.

oliver: Great — let's reconvene after RFC draft. Thanks all.
